chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives'

How many women were made lawful for him? He said: 'Whatever He willed of anything.' I said: The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, 'And [also] a believing woman who dedicates herself to the Prophet' - He said: 'The gift is not lawful except for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); as for other than the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), marriage is not valid except with a dowry.'

I said: What do you make of the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, 'Your wives will not be lawful to you after' - He said: 'He meant by it: The women will not be lawful to you which Allah has forbidden to him in this verse:
Forbidden to you [for marriage] are your mothers, your daughters ... your aunts (paternal) and your aunts (maternal)

And if the matter were as they say, he would have made lawful for you what is not lawful for him, because one of you would replace [whomever he wishes] whenever he wants. And the matter is not as they say; indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made lawful for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to marry from the women whatever he wished, except what He forbade him in this verse in the Surah of Al-Nisa.'

key_terms.أَحْلَلْنَا لَكَ: We have made lawful to you
key_terms.الْهِبَةُ: Gift (specifically of a woman in marriage context)

ai.seo_question: What were the unique marriage privileges of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) compared to other Muslims?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Prophet’s unique privilege of marrying multiple women without limit applied specifically to the exclusions detailed in Surah Al-Nisa, such as close kinship, rather than a general exemption from all marital restrictions. He refutes the notion that the Prophet could marry anyone by citing the specific prohibitions in the same verse, emphasizing that his freedom was bounded by divine law. This hadith underscores the Shia understanding of the Prophet’s distinct legal status (khass) while maintaining continuity with the broader Quranic framework of marriage.
